newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ROBBINS TAKES ONE-STROKE LEAD AT DINAH SHORE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ROBBINS TAKES ONE-STROKE LEAD AT DINAH SHORE.

text.p: Kelly Robbins survived the gusts of wind to take a one-stroke lead at the midway point of the Nabisco Dinah Shore on Friday.
Through 36 holes, she is at seven-under par 137, one stroke ahead of Betsy King, who also shot a 67.
Britain's Laura Davies at one point in her round was tied for the lead. But she made three bogeys and no birdies on her last nine holes and finished three shots behind Robbins.
Robbins, who has five victories on the LPGA, shot a five-under par 67 in the second round on the Dinah Shore Tournament Course at Mission Hills Country Club.

"Believe it or not I'm not hitting the ball all that great," Robbins said. "But I'm getting it on the green and rolling the the ball really great. And I'm not making many mistakes, and when I do I take my medicine. I take my bogey and go on.

"Fortunately I'm hitting it fairly solid, but I don't have the flight I look for. It's solid enough that I'm not losing anything with it. But it doesn't have the draw it normally has and I'm leaving it right. Maybe by Sunday I'll figure it out."
Robbins holed several long putts in equalling the low round of the day.
"I'm probably putting better the last two months than I ever have on tour," she said.
King has 30 career victories, but none since the ShopRite LPGA Classic in 1995, the win that put her into the LPGA Hall of Fame.

"Last year I basically struggled all year," she said. "This is as well as I've played in the last year-and-a-half as far as hitting the ball. Obviously it played pretty tough out there with the wind, but I just played very well."
Fruhwirth, seeking her first LPGA victory, holed an 8-iron from 130 yards for an eagle 2 on the sixth hole, the critical shot in her round of two-under par 70.
"That's a tough green to putt, but I didn't have to putt," she said.
